cases.description: Request 1 as deterministic CBOR in a request event addressed to the mailbox key; one reply event by that key carrying the envelope. A reply, and every required envelope property PASS: row 7 of the profile's §8.1.

cases.description: A limit of two replies by content, and three reply events naming request event 1, each signed by a key the request did not address and each carrying a distinct genuine envelope for request 1. The first two are replies by content. The first, delivered again, is one event and uses no more of the limit. The mailbox key's own reply after the limit is used is still a reply. The third is beyond the limit and is not verified: not a reply, also when it claims the first one's id, since events are counted by their recomputed hash. caller_invariance PASS over the three replies.

cases.description: A reply event naming request event 2, signed by a key the request did not address, carrying the responder's genuine envelope for request 1. Check 7 fails and the content does not bind this request: not a reply; a recorded absence at the deadline. A relay cannot turn the request into a response received and failed.
Reply event 1 with its id intact and its signature replaced by another event's. Check 6 (signature) fails; the content is still the responder's envelope for this request: a reply by content.

cases.description: Reply event 1 with its content replaced, after signing, by an envelope under a key the trust policy does not accept. Check 5 (id) fails and the content proves nothing: not a reply; a recorded absence at the deadline.

The relay delivers reply event 1, unchanged, on request 2's subscription. Its e tag names request event 1: check 2 (reply_to) fails, so it is not a reply to this request; a recorded absence at the deadline.

A relay alters request event 1 on its way to the responder: once with its id kept over request 2's octets, once with the id recomputed. The responder checks each request event before answering, ignores both (id, then signature), and sends no reply: the requester records an absence at the deadline, never a response received and failed.
No event arrives before the deadline. The requester records an absence whose window closes at the request's deadline and whose route is the mailbox it addressed.

No event arrives before the deadline, and the requester records an absence. Then the relay delivers reply event 1, which it had delayed past the deadline. The absence record is unchanged; the late event is a reply that verifies as in mailbox-exchange, kept as its own later fact that cites the request by its digest and its event id.
